paper_title: Reconfigurations of Plane Caterpillars and Paths (Poster Abstract)
statement: Next, we consider the case when S is a point set in general position. For a caterpillar C ∈ C(S), and consecutive spine vertices vi , . . . , vj of C, we write Si,j for the point set consisting of the spine vertices and all of the leaves attached to them. We call C ∈ C(S) with spine v1 , v2 , . . . , vk a well-separated caterpillar if for each i ≥ 1, the convex hull of S1,i is disjoint from the rest of S. We can prove that all caterpillars in this class are mutually connected in Gslide C (S). This large connected component is significant, as we can also show slide that GC (S) is disconnected. On the other hand, we can prove that the rotation graph emp-rot Grot C (S) is connected. We leave open the question of the connectivity of GC .
context: ▶ Theorem 2. Let S be a set of n ≥ 3 points in convex position in the plane. Then, the graph Gcomp-flip C (S) is connected with diameter at most 2n − 5. Any two well-separated caterpillars are connected in Gslide C (S). ▶ Theorem 4. The graph Gslide C (S) is connected for every set S of n points in the plane if n ≤ 7. If n ≥ 8, there exists a set S of n points such that Gslide C (S) has isolated vertices.
